triage.name: Anxiety
triage.reason: A common psychiatric presentation with somatic complaints; diagnosis is reached by history and ruling out mimics, and it teaches interview skills.

demographics: Generalized anxiety and phobias are more common in women; social anxiety is roughly equal between men and women
Often first seen in primary care rather than by a mental health clinician

risk_factors.text: Family history of anxiety or another mental disorder
Traumatic or stressful life events, including in childhood
Shy, withdrawn temperament or behavioral inhibition in new situations
Ongoing life stress such as job, school, financial, or relationship strain

comorbidities: Substance use, especially alcohol or sedatives
Asthma or other chronic medical illness
family_history: Anxiety disorder in a parent or sibling
Depression or another mental disorder in the family
social_history: Recent or ongoing stressors at work, school, or home
Limited social support or recent loss
Alcohol or cannabis use to calm down
exposures: Stimulants such as caffeine, nicotine, or decongestants

chief_complaints.text: I can't stop worrying about everything
I feel tense and on edge all the time
My heart races and I feel like something bad is going to happen
I can't sleep because my mind won't shut off

hpi.onset: Gradual, often building over months; many patients date it to a stressful period or a major life change
hpi.duration: Weeks to years; by the time it is diagnosed, symptoms have usually been present most days for at least several months
hpi.progression: Chronic and fluctuating, worse during stressful periods and better during calmer ones; it rarely resolves on its own without treatment
hpi.location: Not localized; described as a whole-body feeling of tension
hpi.quality: Persistent worry that feels hard to control, with a physical sense of restlessness and tension
hpi.severity: Mild to moderate for most; can be severe enough to interfere with work, school, sleep, and relationships
hpi.timing: Most days, often worse in the evening or when trying to fall asleep
aggravating: Stress at work, school, or home
Crowds or being far from home
relieving: Alcohol or other substances (patients often report this, though it worsens things over time)

associated_symptoms.text: Muscle tension, especially neck, shoulders, or jaw
Trouble concentrating or mind going blank
Shortness of breath or a smothering feeling
Sweating, trembling, or a churning stomach
Avoiding situations that trigger the worry

pertinent_negatives: Chest pain that comes on with exertion and resolves with rest
Heat intolerance with tremor and weight loss
New focal weakness, numbness, or trouble speaking
Hearing voices or having thoughts others are out to get them
Using a substance every day and feeling sick without it
Symptoms that only occur after a specific substance or medication

argues_against: Chest pain that reliably comes with exertion and eases with rest

positives.text: Feeling like I can't get a full breath

argues_against: Shortness of breath with wheeze that responds to an inhaler

positives.text: Muscle tension in the neck and shoulders

negatives: New weakness in an arm or leg
Numbness or weakness on one side

positives.text: Worry that is hard to control
Avoiding things that trigger the worry
Low mood or loss of interest

negatives: Thoughts of harming myself or others
Feeling that others are plotting against me
argues_against: Mania with decreased need for sleep and racing thoughts

atypical.how_it_differs: Young children often show anxiety as stomachaches, headaches, clinginess, tantrums, or refusal to go to school rather than describing worry in words.
missing_classic_features: Insight that the worry is out of proportion

atypical.how_it_differs: Anxiety often shows up as physical complaints, poor sleep, or agitation, and is frequently mixed with depression or early cognitive changes; medical causes and medication side effects are more likely.
missing_classic_features: Reporting worry as the main problem
Clear onset during a stressful life period

atypical.how_it_differs: Worry often centers on the pregnancy, the baby's health, and childbirth, and physical symptoms overlap with normal pregnancy changes.
missing_classic_features: Symptoms clearly separate from pregnancy-related body changes

general.mild: Alert, well-groomed, cooperative; appears mildly tense but comfortable
general.moderate: Restless, fidgeting, wringing hands, leg bouncing; speech may be rapid
general.severe: Markedly agitated or tremulous, diaphoretic, visibly distressed, may have trouble staying seated
general.critical: Extreme agitation or panic, hyperventilating, diaphoretic, appears terrified; unable to participate in exam

findings.maneuver: Observe the patient's demeanor and affect during the interview
findings.finding: Anxious, apprehensive, or tense affect; appears worried or on edge

findings.maneuver: Observe the patient's motor activity during the visit
findings.finding: Restlessness, fidgeting, hand wringing, foot tapping, or difficulty sitting still

findings.maneuver: Listen to the patient's spontaneous speech
findings.finding: Speech is normal in rate, rhythm, and volume without pressured quality or flight of ideas

findings.maneuver: Assess the organization and flow of the patient's thoughts during history
findings.finding: Thought process is linear and goal-directed without loosening of associations

findings.maneuver: Ask about hearing voices, seeing things others do not, or feeling that others are plotting against them
Ask directly about thoughts of harming oneself or others
findings.finding: No suicidal or homicidal ideation, intent, or plan

findings.maneuver: Assess orientation to person, place, time, and situation
findings.finding: Oriented to person, place, time, and situation; attention and concentration grossly intact

findings.maneuver: Palpate the trapezius and paraspinal muscles of the neck and shoulders
findings.finding: Muscle tightness or tenderness in the neck and shoulders

findings.maneuver: Ask the patient to hold both arms outstretched with fingers spread
findings.finding: Fine postural tremor of the hands
Cool, clammy, or sweaty palms and skin

findings.maneuver: Palpate the thyroid gland while the patient swallows
Inspect the eyes for proptosis and lid lag
Auscultate the heart in the sitting and supine positions
findings.finding: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, rubs, or gallops
Clear breath sounds without wheezes, crackles, or prolonged expiration

findings.maneuver: Perform a focused neurologic exam including cranial nerves, strength, sensation, and coordination
findings.finding: No focal motor, sensory, or cranial nerve deficits

findings.maneuver: Inspect the neck for visible thyroid enlargement

labs.caveat: Hyperthyroidism can mimic anxiety with palpitations, tremor, heat intolerance, and weight loss; a suppressed TSH with high free T4 points to thyroid disease rather than an anxiety disorder.
Ordered when TSH is low to confirm thyrotoxicosis.
Hypoglycemia can cause palpitations, tremor, and a sense of dread; check if symptoms occur fasting or with diabetes treatment.
Negative. In a patient who could be pregnant, a positive result changes the differential and limits medication choices.
Only when features suggest Cushing syndrome (weight gain, striae, easy bruising, proximal weakness).
Not a cause of anxiety; screens for diabetes when symptoms overlap or before starting some medications.
Baseline renal function before starting a medication that is renally cleared.
Hyponatremia can present with confusion, restlessness, or anxiety; consider if the patient takes a diuretic or SSRI.
Hypercalcemia can cause anxiety, confusion, and fatigue.

findings.finding: No ischemic ST-segment changes, no arrhythmia, and no conduction abnormality

findings.text: Normal heart size and clear lungs

imaging.preferred_when: Only when pulmonary embolism is suspected (sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, hypoxia, tachycardia, or a positive D-dimer)

findings.text: No filling defect in the pulmonary arteries

imaging.preferred_when: Only when a structural brain cause is suspected (new focal deficit, seizure, or altered mental status)

initial.why: Thyroid disease is the most common medical mimic of anxiety
Anemia can cause palpitations, fatigue, and dyspnea
Electrolyte and glucose abnormalities can mimic anxiety
Pregnancy changes the differential and treatment choices
Evaluates palpitations, tachycardia, or chest symptoms and looks for arrhythmia
initial.only_if: palpitations, chest pain, or tachycardia are prominent

confirmatory.why: Structured assessment of worry, panic attacks, avoidance, and functional impairment establishes the diagnosis and the specific anxiety disorder

supporting.why: Confirms thyrotoxicosis when TSH is low
Screens for diabetes when symptoms overlap or before starting medication
Baseline renal function before starting a renally cleared medication
Screens for a urinary cause when urinary frequency or dysuria is prominent

not_indicated.why: Not needed unless pulmonary embolism is suspected
not_indicated.only_if: pulmonary embolism is suspected (sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, hypoxia, or tachycardia)

not_indicated.why: Not needed without focal neurologic findings, seizure, or altered mental status
not_indicated.only_if: a structural brain cause is suspected (new focal deficit, seizure, or altered mental status)

not_indicated.why: No role in the routine workup of anxiety
Not indicated unless chest pain suggests acute coronary syndrome
Not routine; reserve for suspected pulmonary disease
not_indicated.only_if: respiratory symptoms or an abnormal lung exam suggest pulmonary disease

not_indicated.why: No role in the routine workup of anxiety
No role in the routine workup of anxiety
Not indicated unless abdominal pain suggests pancreatitis
Not routine; consider only if neurologic findings or a dietary deficiency is suspected
Not routine; consider only if anemia is found on CBC

decision_points: Rule out medical mimics (thyroid disease, arrhythmia, substance or medication effects) before diagnosing a primary anxiety disorder
Ask directly about suicidal ideation and safety at every visit
Pregnancy test before starting medication in anyone who could be pregnant
Do not order chest imaging or cardiac testing unless the history or exam points to a cardiopulmonary cause

criteria.name: Generalized anxiety disorder
criteria.summary: Excessive worry that is hard to control, occurring more days than not for at least 6 months, with at least three of: restlessness or feeling keyed up, being easily fatigued, trouble concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, and sleep disturbance. The worry causes distress or impairment and is not due to a substance, medication, or another medical condition.

criteria.name: Panic disorder
criteria.summary: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks followed by at least one month of persistent concern about further attacks or their consequences, or a maladaptive change in behavior related to the attacks.

criteria.name: Social anxiety disorder
criteria.summary: Marked fear or anxiety about one or more social situations in which the person may be scrutinized, with fear of showing anxiety symptoms or being negatively evaluated. The situations are avoided or endured with intense fear, and the fear is out of proportion to the actual threat.

differential.name: Hyperthyroidism
differential.why_considered: Palpitations, tremor, restlessness, heat intolerance, and weight loss overlap closely with anxiety
differential.trigger: Palpitations with tremor, heat intolerance, weight loss, or a goiter

history: Weight loss despite a good appetite
Heat intolerance and increased sweating
Diarrhea or frequent stools
Symptoms that are constant rather than tied to stress
exam: Fine tremor that persists at rest
labs: Suppressed TSH with elevated free T4 or T3

differential.name: Cardiac arrhythmia
differential.why_considered: Palpitations and a racing heartbeat are common anxiety complaints, and paroxysmal arrhythmias can be mistaken for panic attacks
differential.trigger: Palpitations that start and stop abruptly, syncope, or a family history of sudden death

history: Abrupt onset and offset of palpitations
Palpitations at rest or during sleep
Near-fainting or fainting
Known structural heart disease
exam: Irregular pulse or a rate that does not match the reported distress
Signs of heart failure such as jugular venous distension or edema
imaging: ECG showing atrial fibrillation, supraventricular tachycardia, or another arrhythmia
Echocardiogram showing structural disease when indicated

differential.name: Pulmonary embolism
differential.why_considered: Sudden shortness of breath, chest tightness, and tachycardia can look like a panic attack
differential.trigger: Sudden dyspnea with pleuritic chest pain, hypoxia, or tachycardia out of proportion to distress

history: Sudden onset rather than a build-up over months
Pleuritic chest pain worse with deep breath
Recent surgery, immobility, or a prior clot
Active cancer or estrogen use
exam: Unilateral leg swelling or calf tenderness
imaging: Filling defect in the pulmonary arteries on CT pulmonary angiogram

differential.name: Substance or medication-induced anxiety
differential.why_considered: Caffeine, stimulants, decongestants, steroids, and alcohol or sedative withdrawal all produce anxiety symptoms
differential.trigger: Symptoms that began or worsened after a substance, medication, or a period of heavy use

history: Heavy caffeine, energy drink, or stimulant use
New medication such as albuterol, prednisone, or levothyroxine
Alcohol or sedative use with tremor and sweats when stopping
Temporal link between the substance and the symptoms
exam: Tremor, diaphoresis, and tachycardia during withdrawal
labs: Urine drug screen positive for stimulants or other substances

differential.name: Major depressive disorder
differential.why_considered: Depression and anxiety commonly occur together, and both cause poor sleep, poor concentration, and irritability

history: Persistent low mood or loss of interest most of the day
Guilt, hopelessness, or thoughts of death
Anxiety symptoms that began after the mood symptoms
exam: Flat or sad affect rather than tense and apprehensive

differential.name: Generalized anxiety disorder
differential.why_considered: The index condition itself; the differential workup must confirm that the worry is not better explained by another disorder

history: Excessive worry about several areas that is hard to control, more days than not for at least 6 months
At least three of restlessness, easy fatigue, poor concentration, irritability, muscle tension, and sleep disturbance
No discrete panic attacks or a single feared situation
exam: Anxious, apprehensive affect with normal speech and thought process
labs: Normal TSH, CBC, and metabolic panel

differential.name: Panic disorder
differential.why_considered: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks with fear of further attacks can be mistaken for generalized anxiety

history: Discrete attacks that peak within minutes
Intense fear of dying, losing control, or going crazy during attacks
At least a month of worry about further attacks or avoidance
exam: Symptoms are episodic and the exam is normal between attacks

differential.name: Social anxiety disorder
differential.why_considered: Fear of scrutiny and avoidance of social situations overlaps with generalized worry

history: Fear limited to social or performance situations
Fear of embarrassment or negative evaluation
Avoidance of speaking, eating, or performing in front of others
exam: Anxiety appears only when discussing social situations

differential.name: Irritable bowel syndrome
differential.why_considered: Anxiety and IBS frequently coexist, and both cause abdominal discomfort and altered stool habits

history: Recurrent abdominal pain related to defecation
Change in stool frequency or form
Symptoms relieved by defecation
exam: Mild diffuse abdominal tenderness without peritoneal signs
labs: Normal CBC, CRP, and celiac serology when ordered

severity.mild: Worry most days that is bothersome but does not limit work, school, or relationships; sleep and appetite are largely intact
severity.moderate: Worry is hard to control and causes clear distress or impairment at work, school, or home; sleep disturbance, muscle tension, and avoidance are present
severity.severe: Pervasive worry with marked functional impairment, frequent panic symptoms, poor sleep, and difficulty leaving home or completing daily tasks
severity.critical: Extreme agitation or a prolonged panic state with hyperventilation, diaphoresis, and inability to participate in the exam; assess for suicidal ideation and consider a medical cause

red_flags.meaning: A psychiatric emergency requiring immediate safety planning and evaluation

red_flags.finding: New focal weakness, numbness, trouble speaking, or seizure
red_flags.meaning: Suggests a structural neurologic cause rather than a primary anxiety disorder

red_flags.finding: Sudden dyspnea with pleuritic chest pain, hypoxia, or tachycardia out of proportion to distress
red_flags.meaning: Consider pulmonary embolism or another acute cardiopulmonary cause
Consider an arrhythmia or structural heart disease

red_flags.finding: Weight loss, heat intolerance, or tremor with a goiter
Symptoms that began after a substance, medication, or during withdrawal

complications.name: Major depressive disorder
clues: Persistent low mood or loss of interest

complications.name: Substance use disorder
clues: Alcohol or sedative use to calm down

complications.name: Functional impairment and lost productivity
clues: Avoidance of social or occupational activities

special_populations.differences: Young children often show anxiety as stomachaches, headaches, clinginess, tantrums, or refusal to attend school rather than describing worry in words; involve parents and school in the assessment.

Anxiety often presents as physical complaints, poor sleep, or agitation and is frequently mixed with depression or early cognitive changes; medical causes and medication side effects are more likely, so review the medication list carefully.

Worry often centers on the pregnancy, the baby's health, and childbirth, and physical symptoms overlap with normal pregnancy changes; check pregnancy status before starting medication and weigh risks and benefits with the patient.

key_questions.question: Tell me about your worry — what kinds of things do you worry about, and how much of the day is it on your mind?
key_questions.looking_for: Worry about several different areas (health, money, work, family) that is excessive and hard to control, present most days

key_questions.question: How long has this been going on?
key_questions.looking_for: Most days for at least 6 months; shorter duration or a clear recent trigger points elsewhere

key_questions.question: Is the worry there all the time, or does it come in sudden attacks that peak within minutes?
key_questions.looking_for: Continuous background worry suggests generalized anxiety; discrete attacks peaking within minutes suggest panic attacks

key_questions.question: Does the worry or the physical symptoms get in the way of work, school, or your relationships?
key_questions.looking_for: Distress or functional impairment, which is required to call it a disorder rather than a normal reaction

key_questions.question: How is your sleep?
key_questions.looking_for: Trouble falling or staying asleep because the mind will not shut off

key_questions.question: Do you feel restless, keyed up, or on edge?
key_questions.looking_for: Restlessness or feeling wound up

key_questions.question: Do you notice muscle tension, especially in your neck, shoulders, or jaw?
key_questions.looking_for: Muscle tension, jaw clenching, or grinding

key_questions.question: How is your concentration?
key_questions.looking_for: Trouble concentrating or the mind going blank

key_questions.question: Do you feel irritable or easily tired?
key_questions.looking_for: Irritability and easy fatigability

key_questions.question: Do you have palpitations, shortness of breath, dizziness, sweating, or stomach upset?
key_questions.looking_for: Physical symptoms of anxiety; also helps separate a primary anxiety disorder from a medical mimic

key_questions.question: Are there situations you now avoid because of the worry?
key_questions.looking_for: Avoidance of crowds, driving, social situations, or leaving home

key_questions.question: Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you used to enjoy?
key_questions.looking_for: Coexisting depression, which is common and changes treatment

key_questions.question: Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that you would be better off dead?
key_questions.looking_for: Suicidal ideation, intent, or plan — a psychiatric emergency

key_questions.question: Do you hear voices, see things others do not, or feel that people are plotting against you?
key_questions.looking_for: Absent; psychosis points to a different diagnosis

key_questions.question: Have you had any new weakness, numbness, trouble speaking, or a seizure?
key_questions.looking_for: Absent; focal neurologic findings suggest a structural cause

key_questions.question: Have you ever had chest pain with exertion that eases with rest, or fainting?
key_questions.looking_for: Absent; present suggests a cardiac cause rather than anxiety

key_questions.question: Have you had weight loss despite a normal appetite, heat intolerance, or diarrhea?
key_questions.looking_for: Absent; present suggests hyperthyroidism

key_questions.question: How much caffeine do you take in — coffee, tea, energy drinks, soda?
key_questions.looking_for: Heavy caffeine or stimulant use that could be driving the symptoms

key_questions.question: How much alcohol, cannabis, or other substances do you use, and do you use them to calm down?
key_questions.looking_for: Substance use or withdrawal as a cause, or self-medication

key_questions.question: What medications and supplements do you take, including any inhalers or steroids?
key_questions.looking_for: Albuterol, levothyroxine, prednisone, methylphenidate, amphetamine, or bupropion that can cause or worsen anxiety

key_questions.question: Has a doctor ever told you that you have a thyroid problem or a heart rhythm problem?
key_questions.looking_for: Thyroid disease or arrhythmia as a medical mimic

key_questions.question: Does anyone in your family have anxiety, depression, or another mental health condition?
key_questions.looking_for: Family history of anxiety or another mental disorder

key_questions.question: What has been going on in your life lately — work, school, money, relationships, or any losses?
key_questions.looking_for: Ongoing stressors or a recent traumatic event

key_questions.question: Could you be pregnant? When was your last period?
key_questions.looking_for: Pregnancy status, which changes the differential and limits medication choices

reasoning_points: Excessive worry about several areas that the patient finds hard to control, present more days than not for at least 6 months
At least three of restlessness, easy fatigue, poor concentration, irritability, muscle tension, and sleep disturbance
The worry causes distress or clear impairment at work, school, or in relationships
Anxious, apprehensive affect with normal speech, linear thought process, and no psychosis
Suicidal ideation asked about directly and documented
Medical mimics excluded: normal TSH, CBC, and metabolic panel; no goiter, tremor at rest, or focal neurologic deficit
Substances and medications reviewed as possible causes (caffeine, stimulants, decongestants, steroids, alcohol or sedative withdrawal)
Coexisting depression screened for with a validated tool such as the GAD-7 and PHQ-9

easy: Young adult with months of worry about several areas, trouble sleeping, and muscle tension
Classic anxious affect with normal speech and thought process
Normal TSH and no medical red flags
Clear functional impairment described in the patient's own words
medium: Prominent physical symptoms (palpitations, shortness of breath, dizziness) that raise a cardiac or pulmonary concern
Heavy caffeine or stimulant use that could explain the symptoms
Anxiety mixed with depression, making it unclear which came first
Older adult whose anxiety shows up as physical complaints and poor sleep
hard: Symptoms that began after a new medication such as albuterol, prednisone, or levothyroxine
Palpitations that start and stop abruptly or occur at rest, suggesting an arrhythmia
Sudden dyspnea with pleuritic chest pain and tachycardia out of proportion to distress
Child who presents with stomachaches, headaches, or school refusal rather than describing worry
Patient with a goiter, weight loss, and heat intolerance suggesting hyperthyroidism
